clue.text: Girl takes in Conservative member about business partner

indicators.note: one thing set about another wraps round it, so the party and member pair encloses the business word
the girl's name takes the rest inside her, so it is split open to hold them

parts.note: a girl's name
standard abbreviation for Conservative
CO is short for company, a business
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A girl's new beau is a Tory MP who also happens to be her business partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business partner' reads as one phrase, but 'business' is wordplay and only 'partner' defines. Two containers nest: the party-and-member pair wraps the business word, and the girl wraps the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is someone who joins with another in an act, usually a crime, so a partner in it.

clue.text: Pulpits where bishop goes into holy book

indicators.note: the bishop's letter travels inside the book's name, splitting it

parts.note: Amos is a book of the Old Testament
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A church picture: the place where the bishop goes to read from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised stand in early Christian churches from which the scriptures were read, a kind of pulpit.

clue.text: Hubbub after union troubled a rich pair of Eastern states

indicators.note: troubled things are stirred up and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these two words rearranged
VA is Virginia and RI is Rhode Island, two states on the US east coast

explanation.surface: Political turmoil after a union is formed, with a rich pair of eastern states unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' sounds political, but here it means a marriage: a charivari was the mock serenade of pots and pans given to newlyweds.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy discordant din banged out outside a newly married couple's home, so a din following a wedding.

clue.text: Manufacture article, managing to set the pace

parts.note: to manufacture is to make
the definite article
running a business is managing it

explanation.surface: A factory owner turning out goods and running the firm, leading the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To make the running is an idiom from racing for leading and dictating the speed that rivals must follow.

clue.text: They cut in, in the dance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: soldiers armed with lances, who pierce with them
second meaning: the ..., a nineteenth-century quadrille

explanation.surface: Dancers who cut in on a couple mid-dance to steal a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut in' looks like the ballroom habit of taking over someone's partner; it is literal cutting, with a lance.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancers were cavalry who stabbed with long spears, and the Lancers is also a set of quadrilles danced by four couples.

clue.text: Blush about supporting illegal acts out East

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after the other
out means the named letter is put out of the word, removed

parts.note: illegal acts are crimes
E is the compass abbreviation, the letter removed
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone colours up when their crimes in the East come out.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'our' is a scan misreading of 'out'. 'Blush' is a verb here, and in a down clue a supporting word sits beneath the one it holds up.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimson is to turn deep red in the face, a verb sense meaning to flush with embarrassment.

clue.text: Old coin and ring left by former pupil

indicators.note: left by something means set down beside it, so these pieces follow the next one

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
a ring is round, like the letter O
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An old schoolboy leaves behind a coin and a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as 'left behind', but it is the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, worth a sixth of a drachma.

clue.text: Black Labrador initially eating uncooked scrap

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the letter swallows the next word

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
uncooked food is raw

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the dog's breed name

parts.note: the opening letter of the breed

explanation.surface: A black Labrador wolfing down a scrap of raw meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a morsel of food for the dog; it means a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is informal for a fight, and a brawl is a rough noisy fight.

clue.text: Confederate following Yankee measure, word for word

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: the American spelling of litre
a confederate is an ally

explanation.surface: A Civil War scene: a Confederate soldier trailing after a Yankee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confederate' and 'Yankee' summon the American Civil War; one is just an ally, the other marks the US spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal translation follows the original exactly, rendering each term in turn without paraphrase.

clue.text: Backing a newspaper is old fashioned

parts.note: backing a cause is being behind it
the London daily that printed this very puzzle

explanation.surface: A complaint that supporting a newspaper is a dated habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is the setter's own paper, a sly joke at its expense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone behind the times has failed to keep up with modern ideas, so is out of date.

clue.text: Instrument of torture concealed in mountain ferns

indicators.note: something concealed in a place is tucked away inside it

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
the rack stretched its victims

explanation.surface: A torture device hidden away among the ferns on a mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken is a large coarse fern that covers hillsides and moorland, a collective noun for the plants.

clue.text: By popular demand? That's not entirely accurate

parts.note: what is popular is in
to exact payment is to demand it

explanation.surface: Doubting a claim that something was done by popular demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just puts the two pieces side by side; the question mark warns that 'popular demand' is not the familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means lacking precision, so something is close but slightly off the mark.

clue.text: Lacking ambition, like a nine-to-five worker, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lazy, without drive or resource
second meaning: someone on fixed office hours works no rota of day and night turns

explanation.surface: A sneer at the unambitious office worker who clocks off at five.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites agreement that office workers are idle; the second reading splits the word into shift and less.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiftless is a standard adjective for lazy and without initiative, and read literally it means having no shifts to work.

clue.text: Layabout escapes from quarrel, disappearing in the opposite direction

indicators.note: the letters are read right to left instead of the usual way
the answer slips out of the run of words that follow, already sitting there

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second run together

explanation.surface: A lazy man slips away from an argument, heading off the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters RELDI straddle 'quarrel' and 'disappearing'; read backwards they spell IDLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is a lazy person who avoids work, which is exactly what an idler does.

clue.text: It sounds like river bait

indicators.note: the answer is said the same way as the word that follows, though spelt differently

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: An angler's riddle about bait for river fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bait' looks like the angler's worm; it is the verb, to torment.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait someone is to taunt or provoke them for amusement, and to tease is the same.

clue.text: Believer accepts blame for health worker

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the believer holds the other word inside

parts.note: a theist believes in God
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: A religious person shoulders the blame for something that went wrong with a nurse or doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats illness or disability, such as a physiotherapist, so is one of many people employed in healthcare.

clue.text: Lad in cosy accommodation belonging to the council

indicators.note: an accommodation is an adjustment or rearrangement made to fit, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the nine letters of these three words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy tucked up in snug lodgings provided by the local council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodation' reads as housing for the lad, but it signals rearranging the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a church council, and synodical is the adjective for what relates to or is decided by one.

clue.text: Dock management providing support for writers

parts.note: to dock a tail is to clip it short
the board of directors manages a company

explanation.surface: The managers of a port backing a group of authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' is the verb to cut short, not the harbour the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipboard is a stiff flat backing with a spring clamp, holding paper firm so people can jot notes on it.

clue.text: Gourmet transformed an initially unappetizing recipe

indicators.note: transformed things change form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: the first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine-dining expert turns a dull recipe into something delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a person devoted to refined pleasure in food and drink, a gourmet by another name.

clue.text: Macmillan accepted this mad role, foolishly

indicators.note: acting foolishly means without order or sense, so the letters scramble

parts.note: the seven letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe that the former prime minister was daft to take on a silly role.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Macmillan, British Prime Minister 1957-63, accepted the title Earl of Stockton in 1984, having long refused a peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: Macmillan took a hereditary peerage late in life, becoming an earl, so the rank of earl is what he took.

clue.text: River spirit raised in African country

indicators.note: in a down clue raising something lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Raising a glass of local liquor by a river somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' tempts with the Niger, which is in the answer, but the wordplay uses the Aire: AIREGIN read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a large nation on the west coast of the continent, with Abuja as its capital.

clue.text: Dangerous atmosphere in borders of Hungary

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the borders are the edges, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters
an atmosphere or aura is an air

explanation.surface: A tense, perilous mood along Hungary's frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is informal for frightening or risky, as in a scary drive along icy roads.

clue.text: Like a layer of wood that's grey

definitions.meaning: first meaning: made of the wood of the ash tree, as a sheet of it would be
second meaning: pale, the colour of ashes

explanation.surface: A sheet of timber described as grey in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen is the old adjective for things made from ash timber, and also describes a pale, drained face.

clue.text: Call demanding attention, on phone in inn

parts.note: ho! is a shout to catch someone's notice
tel is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: A guest phoning reception to demand service in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the call before the phone in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a place offering lodging and meals to travellers, which a hotel also provides.

clue.text: Just competent, but open to correction

parts.note: just means fair, right
competent people are able

explanation.surface: A grudging school report: barely adequate, though willing to improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just competent' reads as faint praise, but 'just' is a separate synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rightable can be put right, so its faults are capable of being amended.

clue.text: Go in for chips without fish at first

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named part is taken away
at first says where the removal happens: the part comes off the front of the word

parts.note: Chips is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter, from the wood shavings
the carp is a freshwater fish, removed from the front

explanation.surface: Ordering chips at the chip shop but skipping the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go in for chips' reads as a trip to the chip shop; 'Chips' is naval slang for the ship's carpenter, and 'at first' says the fish comes off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a building or room is to come into it, so the verb fits the plain sense of going in.

clue.text: Trendy fashion editor gave monotonous performance

parts.note: what is trendy is in
le ton is the fashionable style or set
ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A fashion magazine editor delivering a dull speech.
explanation.walkthrough: TON, the fashionable world, is an old borrowing from French.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to recite in a level chanting voice with little rise or fall, so a flat delivery.

clue.text: Extravagant rise given to worker

parts.note: a ramp is a slope, a rise
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An over-generous pay rise handed to an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' looks like a pay increase; it is an incline.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means unrestrained and growing wildly, sharing the sense of excess and lack of limits.

clue.text: Support removing head, say

indicators.note: taking off the head means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a stalk holds up a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: A stern word about withdrawing backing from the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the noun, as in having one's say.
explanation.definitionFit: Having your say means speaking your mind, and talk is a chance to speak or a conversation.

clue.text: Representative of a thousand fish a fisherman put back

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
the bass is a fish
taken as written

indicators.note: putting back sends the angler's word the other way, right to left

parts.note: a rod is an angler, named after the tackle he fishes with

explanation.surface: An angler throwing back a huge haul of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' sounds like returning the catch to the water; it turns only the angler's word round, while the second 'a' stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a diplomat sent abroad to speak for his or her country, so its official representative.
